title: Support model argument in /gpt-review command
description:
Allow users to pass a model name as an argument to /gpt-review command in PR comments.

Current behavior:
- /gpt-review uses the MODEL env var from workflow config

Desired behavior:
- /gpt-review uses MODEL env var (default)
- /gpt-review gpt-4o uses gpt-4o for this review
- /gpt-review gpt-5.2-pro-2025-12-11 uses that specific model

Implementation:
1. Parse command arguments from comment.body
2. Validate model against supported list
3. Override MODEL env var if valid model provided
4. Pass model to Chat constructor
5. Add error handling for invalid models

Benefits:
- Users can test different models without changing workflow config
- Quick iteration on review quality
- Compare models side-by-side on same PR
close_reason: Implemented in commit ee3c9ec. Users can now pass model as argument to /gpt-review command and use /gpt-review:get-models to see available models.

title: Fix GitHub App to clarify it needs repository variable, not secret
description: The GitHub App was displaying an incorrect error message and the README incorrectly told users to create a 'repository secret'. However, repository secrets CANNOT be read via the GitHub API - they are encrypted and only accessible within GitHub Actions workflows. The GitHub App can only read repository variables (plain text). Fixed the error message and README to clarify this distinction.
close_reason: Fixed in commit d3f6e8d: Clarified that GitHub App needs repository variable (not secret)

title: Add issue_comment event handler for /gpt-review trigger
description:
## Problem

The action only handles `pull_request.opened` and `pull_request.synchronize` events. It does NOT handle `issue_comment` events.

Looking at `src/bot.ts` line 47:
```typescript
app.on(['pull_request.opened', 'pull_request.synchronize'], async (context) => {
```

When triggered via `/gpt-review` comment:
1. Workflow runs with `issue_comment` event
2. Action's Probot handler doesn't match any registered event type
3. Action exits immediately without doing anything

## Expected Behavior

Users should be able to trigger code review on-demand by commenting `/gpt-review` on a PR.

## Proposed Solution

Add an `issue_comment.created` event handler that:
1. Checks if the comment body contains `/gpt-review`
2. Extracts the PR number from `context.payload.issue.number`
3. Fetches PR details and runs the review

## Files to Modify

- `src/bot.ts` - Add issue_comment handler
- `action.yml` - Document the new trigger capability
- `README.md` - Add usage instructions for comment trigger

title: GitHub App token expires on long-running reviews (46+ minutes)
description:
The workflow failed after 46 minutes of processing with 'Bad credentials' (401) when attempting to post the review. GitHub App tokens created by actions/create-github-app-token@v2 expire after 1 hour, but the review processing took too long.

Timeline:
- Started: 11:06:59
- Failed: 12:52:32 (45m 33s elapsed)
- Error: 'Token expired, skipping token revocation'

Root cause: GPT 5.2 Pro with REASONING_EFFORT=high and VERBOSITY=high takes 40s-2min per file. Large PRs with many files exceed the 1-hour token lifetime.

Impact: All review work is lost - the bot processed 74+ files but couldn't post any results.

Solutions:
1. Implement incremental posting - post review comments as they're generated instead of batching at the end
2. Add token refresh logic before posting if elapsed time > 50 minutes
3. Add warning in README about token expiration for large PRs with GPT 5.2 Pro
4. Consider using GITHUB_TOKEN instead of GitHub App token for long-running reviews (doesn't expire during workflow)
5. Add timeout estimation based on file count and model/reasoning_effort
close_reason: Fixed in commit 94ba3e4: Implemented batch posting to prevent token expiration. Reviews now post incrementally every 20 files or 30 minutes, with elapsed time warnings at 40 minutes. Documented limitations and mitigation strategies in README.
